rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: cms.utils.conf.get_templates order is not predictable
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
### Summary

When using `CMS_TEMPLATES_DIR`, the [`cms.utils.conf.get_templates` function](https://github.com/divio/django-cms/blob/006367b6787b1ec884c1e5423a0cfc1a53305328/cms/utils/conf.py#L129) retrieves the list of templates using `os.listdir`, which, [according to the documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.listdir), doesn't guarantee any order. Should there be an `__init__.py` file in the `CMS_TEMPLATES_DIR` listing the available templates, the order is not predictable either on Python 3.5 since dict order is not preserved. This can cause issues, for example [in some 3rd party libraries](https://github.com/nephila/djangocms-apphook-setup/blob/9644a09eefd0d11434f2a70dee92258ef13f1089/djangocms_apphook_setup/base.py#L40) that rely on the templates order.

### Expected behaviour

The list returned by `get_templates` is predictable.

### Actual behaviour

The order of the items in the list is random.

### Environment

* Python version: 3.4
* Django version: 1.11
* django CMS version: 3.5.2

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: feat: Add `FrontendEditableAdminMixin` endpoint to plugins
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

django CMS provides editing endpoints and frontend support for general models through `FrontendEditableAdminMixin`. Specifically, it supports editing a subset of fields only.

This PR extends this feature to plugin models which have no model admin registered for themselves, but are managed by the `PlaceholderAdmin` class. Literally, a few lines of code allow us to have partial editing endpoints for plugins. These can be used for inline editing, for example.

### This PR
* Splits the `FrontendEditableAdminMixin` into two classes, a base class (`BaseEditableAdminMixin`) which provides the endpoint, and a specific class (`FrontendEditableAdmin`) that provides the interface to the model admin.
* The `BaseEditableAdminMixin` is added to the `PlaceholderAdmin` along with the appropriate methods to 
  * retrieve the object being edited
  * find its admin instance (which is its plugin class)
* Tweaks some tricks in the existing `FrontendEditableAdminMixin`:
  * Replaces `get_plugin_name` attributes by callables (makes no difference for the template engine, but does for the plugin class)
  * When changing a plugin, the response does not trigger a page reload but just a local update of the plugin through the data bridge
  * Finally, it provides the placeholder endpoints for plugin models instead of the model admin endpoint (which does not exist for placeholders) in all template tags based on `{% render_model %}

### Usage
With this PR, partial edit can be included by replacing `{{ instance.field }}` in a plugin's template by `{% render_model instance "field" "field,other_field" %}`. Upon double-click this will open a modal with two input fields: `field` and `other_fields`.

Especially interesting is the use of `{% render_model instance "field" "field" %}` which will render the field and allow editing just itself. djangocms-text will take this to inline editing if it is active. See this short demo here on an unstyled blog title field and content fields (**not plugins**):

![inlnie-fields](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e59537bf-e5b7-48ca-a879-ac375b713806)

Any field type can be edited inline if there is an apps (such as djangocms-text) supporting it for that field type. djangocms-text supports `HTMLField` and `CharField`.

### Docs and tests

... are here now.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: Make it possible to use multi-table (concrete) inheritance for Page and Title extensions
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
I just realized that when I have multi-table inheritance for TitleExtension (I guess is the same for PageExtension) and try to publish the page django-cms fails to copy the extension instance and instead save the same instance.

The reason behind this is because `BaseExtension.copy_to_public` method (https://github.com/divio/django-cms/blob/release/3.3.x/cms/extensions/models.py#L64-L87) does not nullify pk fields of parent model(s).

I'm using Django 1.8 and DjangoCMS 3.3.

I created a workaround in my project which involves overwriting whole  `copy_to_public` method without calling `super` which is totally bad thing (If I want to upgrade the CMS in the future).

I can prepare e PR with proposed solution.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: fix: Replaced `languages` field from `Page` which used to become inconsistent
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

This PR removes the ambiguous `languages` field from the `Page` model:
* Together with djangocms-versioning the field's content becomes ambiguous
* It tends to become inconsistent over time (#8019)
* It's size limit effectively but unnecessarily restricts the number of languages usable.

Originally, it contained a chained string of available `Title` objects (which is of course redundant) and was maintained to save database hits. With django CMS 4 its use does not save database hits any more. The same information is available through the new `PageUrl` model, which needs to be unique by page and language.

Fixes #8019 
Fixes #7838 

## Related resources

Remove the `languages` field from the `Page` model to address inconsistencies and redundancy issues. Replace it with a more reliable mechanism using the `PageUrl` model, which ensures unique page-language combinations. Enhancements:
- Deprecate and replace the `languages` attribute and related methods with a more reliable mechanism using `PageUrl`.

nodes.title: [BUG] Model PageUrl should add constraint unique_together
nodes.body:
## Description

Each CMS `Page` can have one `PageUrl` object per language. If there are more than that, a `MultipleObjectsReturned`-exception may be raised.


## Steps to reproduce

* Edit the page which is set as Home.
* Save the content.
* Publish that page.

The `PageUrl`-object for the home page now has two entries in the database. Reason is this 
https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/21d6a6defc5a6321bd691e43eb57c112508b952f/cms/models/pagemodel.py#L292-L296
code snippet. Here `new_path` is a functional expression containing `Concat(ConcatPair(Value('parent_slug'), ConcatPair(Value('/'), F(slug))))`. Since the resulting `path` field of the home page must be an empty string the above query can't work.

## Alternative reproduction

* Create a page with a named slug and publish as a subpage of another page. 
* Create another page with the same slug, but as child of another parent page.
* Move one of those pages so that they become siblings.

Now we get two objects of `PageUrl` with the same `language` and the same `path` entry for different pages. This in my opinion is inconsistent.

I therefore strongly recommend to add `unique_together = [['path', 'language'], ['page', 'language']]` to the `Meta`-class of the `PageUrl`-class.

In my setup I already did this. This is how I found out about the two errors reported before. Otherwise I rarely ran into the problem of hitting a `MultipleObjectsReturned`-exception, whose real cause then of course is much harder to detect.


## Do you want to help fix this issue?

* [x] Yes, I want to help fix this issue and I will join #workgroup-pr-review on [Slack](https://www.django-cms.org/slack) to confirm with the community that a PR is welcome. 
* [ ] No, I only want to report the issue.

I already patched this locally and would like to know if that proposed model change makes sense.

I currently have no receipt to reproduce this, but apparently we have an inconsistency in our database regarding the field `languages` in model `Page`.

This currently is not reproducible, but I can explain what is happening using the Django shell:

```
>>> from cms.models.pagemodel import *

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: Deprecation Warnings
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
### Summary

There are a lot of deprecation warnings when running on django 1.10, which django CMS supports. It would probably be a good idea to clean those up. 

### Expected behaviour

no deprecation warnings

### Actual behaviour

Lots of warnings. Note: since django 1.10, you have to run python with `-Wd` to see the warnings. Might be a good idea to do that when running the tests suite.

Here's a list of all the warnings:

1. "Importing from `django.core.urlresolvers` is deprecated in favor of `django.urls`".
    - This is done in several places.
2. "on_delete will be a required arg for `OneToOneField` in Django 2.0. Set it to `models.CASCADE` on models and in existing migrations if you want to maintain the current default behavior." 
    - This warning happens all over the place. 
    - To fix, every `ForeignKey` in all existing migrations need to set `on_delete=models.CASCADE` if they do not already specify `on_delete`. Then, set `on_delete=models.CASCADE` on all `ForeignKey`'s in all models, unless cascade is not the intended behavior. If the behavior should be different, new migrations will need to be created after changing  the models. 
3. "Managers from concrete parents will soon qualify as default managers. As a result, the 'objects' manager won't be created (or recreated) automatically anymore on 'cms.PageUserGroup' and 'objects' declared on 'auth.Group' will be promoted to default manager. You can declare explicitly `objects = models.Manager()` on 'PageUserGroup' to keep things the way they are or you can switch to the new behavior right away by setting `Meta.manager_inheritance_from_future` to `True`."
    - This only happens once from what I can tell, but the warning is pretty self-explanatory.

There could probably be more warnings. These are only the ones I see when I run my own test suite on my own project which uses django CMS.

nodes.title: Similar field names with PageUser and my custom user model
nodes.body:
I have a similar problem as @jrief describes in #3973.
We use django 1.8.2 with a custom user Model and as i tried to install django-cms 3.1.1 i got the following error:

```
django.core.exceptions.FieldError: Local field 'created_by' in class 'PageUser' clashes with field of similar name from base class 'Contact'
```

Unfortunately my custom User model already has a `created_by` Field. And [django does not allow to override any Field attribute from the parent Model](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/topics/db/models/#field-name-hiding-is-not-permitted).

Since the PageUser model does not add any logic rather than the `created_by` Field, the best solution for me would be to swap the PageUser model like django does with `auth.User`. Are there any Plans to support that functionality? If not, i could invest some time and send a PR.

Or anyone else ran into the same problem and can give a hint?

nodes.title: The fields `created_by` of PageUser, PageGroup and `user`/`group` of PagePermission can cause unwanted user/group deletion
nodes.body:
## Description

As all of these fields are defined as `on_delete=models.CASCADE`. That means, if I delete User A, that has previously created a `PageUser` B, the user B will be deleted as well. I never was really sure what these are anyway... see also #5517 .

## Steps to reproduce

Create User A. Log in with A, create PageUser B. Delete User A. User B is gone as well.

## Expected behaviour

User B should not be deleted. Instead, one could show (deleted User), and define the fields as `on_delete=models.SET_NULL`. Or remove the fields completly.

## Actual behaviour

User B is gone/deleted.   

Also, discovered that normal new Users that are created trigger the creation of a `PageUser`, if `CMS_PERMISSION` is true. This can cause confusion, and makes it almost impossible to delete useres on such a system.

for discussion since 2016 #5517

Copying and pasting an unpublished page renders the page tree and thereby the whole cms unusable. `./manage.py cms fix-tree` will not repair this tree.

## Description

http://docs.django-cms.org/en/latest/contributing/development-policies.html#reporting-security-issues

Steps:
1.	Start from empty project with `./manage.py migrate`, `./manage.py createsuperuser`, and `./manage.py runserver`

Page tree breaks with message “Error: Could not load node”. Switching languages does not help. The server reports an server error when serving `/admin/cms/pagecontent/get-tree/`.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: feat: Improved editing response time by global caching of plugin restrictions
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

Plugin restrictions need to be recalculated on every request in edit and structure mode. This is of n² complexity (n: number of plugins). 

While the plugin restrictions can be widely customized, the standard implementation respects the `CMS_PLACEHOLDER_CONF` setting allowing restrictions to depend on template and slot names.

This PR caches these restriction globally in the plugin pool for all plugins that follow the standard implementation.

Request times reduce by 30 to 50% in edit mode.

Logic does not change (only its implementation)- tests remain the same.

## Related resources

## Summary by Sourcery

Implements global caching of plugin restrictions to improve editing response time. It introduces a cache for plugin restrictions that depend only on the template and placeholder slot, and a decorator to mark methods that support this caching strategy.

New Features:
- Introduces global caching of plugin restrictions based on template and placeholder slot, significantly improving the response time when editing plugins.

Enhancements:
- Adds a decorator `template_slot_caching` to indicate that a plugin's method supports global caching based on placeholder slots and templates.
- Improves the performance of `page_getter` by directly querying `PageContent` to avoid separate queries for source and page.

## Summary by Sourcery

This pull request introduces global caching of plugin restrictions to improve editing response time. It introduces a cache for plugin restrictions that depend only on the template and placeholder slot, and a decorator to mark methods that support this caching strategy.

New Features:

Enhancements:
- Adds a decorator `template_slot_caching` to indicate that a plugin's method supports global caching based on placeholder slots and templates.
- Improves the performance of `page_getter` by directly querying `PageContent` to avoid separate queries for source and page.

By default the cms will render draft pages unless the user explicitly enables preview mode.
Preview mode persists across requests via a session flag.

`?preview` enables preview mode (public only pages) and disables edit mode
`?edit` enables edit mode and disables preview mode
`?edit_off` disables edit mode

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
FIPS[0] is not a support crytographic function on FIPS compliant
systems, and is thus disabled.  Moving md5 hashing to use sha256, we can
use django-cms on FIPS compliant systems.

Test updated to include new function output.

[0] http://csrc.nist.gov/groups/STM/cmvp/documents/140-1/140val-all.htm

### Summary

On FIPS enabled systems, md5() functions are not available.  Moving to sha256, django-cms can be used.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: feat: Improved delete page confirmation message
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body: ## Description When selecting "Delete page..." from either the toolbar menu or in the page tree, a confirmation message is shown detailing which objects will be deleted. This used to be the standard Django delete confirmation message, which lists each instance of objects to be deleted, including each single page, page content, page url, version, plugin, version state tracking, plugin and other objects. As a result, the delete confirmation is often not seen as important or relevant to the user. To improve UX, this PR proposes a **simplified delete confirmation for pages** only. * In the summary, it lists the number of pages, page contents and plugins that will be deleted. * As details, it contains the hierarchical page tree including page and page content objects. **All other models are not explicitly listed.** ## Screenshot (djangocms-admin-style hides the summary, unfortunately, but it renders nicely in plain Django admin or with djangocms-simple-admin-style) (With https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/pull/8067, the (bold) page titles will appear in the form of "My page title (/path/to/page)") Feedback welcome (@jrief, @marksweb, @vinitkumar). ## Related resources * #7984 * #7748 ## Checklist * [x] I have opened this pull request against ``develop-4`` * [ ] I have added or modified the tests when changing logic * [x] I have followed [the conventional commits guidelines](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) to add meaningful information into the changelog * [x] I have read the [contribution guidelines ](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.rst) and I have joined the channel #pr-reviews on our [Discord Server](https://discord-pr-review-channel.django-cms.org) to find a “pr review buddy” who is going to review my pull request.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: Potential performance optimization for fetching Page titles
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
Hi everyone, sorry for not using a template but this is not for a bug template.

I have a technical question regarding performance optimizations for CMS. I’ve noticed that retrieving titles of the pages are not optimized and I’m wondering is there a reason why it was implemented like this. Here is an example:

`[page.get_title() for page in Page.objects.filter(id__in=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])]`

Creates 8 queries to the database, but if you add a prefetch_related to the query set it also does 8+1 queries (one is for retrieving all the titles for these pages):

`[page.get_title() for page in Page.objects.prefetch_related("title_set").filter(id__in=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])]`

This can be optimized if we change the way the title cache is populated on the line:
https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/develop/cms/models/pagemodel.py#L1434.

Instead of doing
`titles = Title.objects.filter(page=self)`
we could do
`titles = self.title_set.all()`

And this will create only two queries, and the number of queries won’t increase linearly with the number of pages.
I’m wondering is there a reason why titles are fetched this way?

I could create a PR if DjangoCMS core contributors agree on the change.

nodes.title: Support for Django template engine subclasses
nodes.body:
https://github.com/divio/django-cms/blob/release/3.4.x/cms/utils/setup.py#L21

``` python

    try:
        django_backend = [x for x in settings.TEMPLATES
                          if x['BACKEND'] == 'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates'][0]
    except IndexError:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured("django CMS requires django.template.context_processors.request in "
                                   "'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates' context processors.")
```

This is insane! You forbid usage of customized engines.

Why don't you check if `django.template.context_processors.request` is in the list of `context_processors` instead?

``` python

    if 'django.template.context_processors.request' not in x['OPTIONS']['context_processors']:
         raise ImproperlyConfigured("django CMS requires django.template.context_processors.request in "
                                    "'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates' context processors.")
```

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
Sometimes a plugin can cause an exception based on whatever is entered by the user, or because of other causes (e.g an api that is unreachable). Obviously this is a bug in the plugin, but it can happen and it can happen on production servers. Currently we let the exception bubble up and show a 500 page. In production this is a desaster, because with frontend editing, you can't even navigate the the page and remove the offending plugin anymore. The user is completely blocked concerning that page and has to get a developer to fix the bug before any more content can be entered on the page.

I propose that plugin rendering for each plugin has a try/except around it. To Visitors the offending plugin should just not be rendered (or an error message?). To content editors the plugin should be rendered in a way that is clear that something went wrong (perhaps with a red border and a message in the notification area at the top of the screen). In structure view the plugin should also be highlighted. In any case it should be possible to still edit or remove the plugin.
In any case the error should be logged with a traceback.

This behaviour should be controlled by a new setting that uses `DEBUG` as a default but can be overridden.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: [BUG] Admin UI Text in Page Global Permissions is Unclear
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body: ## Description Admin UI text in Page Global Permissions has unclear meanings. [Original report.](https://django-cmsworkspace.slack.com/archives/C01EBCEK49E/p1692654745963519) ## Steps to reproduce ### "View restricted" 1. Go to '`/admin/cms/globalpagepermissions/add`. 2. Find "on page level" (fields description) > "View restricted" (checkbox label). ### "frontend view restriction" 1. Go to '`/admin/cms/globalpagepermissions/add`. 2. Find "on page level" (fields description) > "View restricted" (checkbox label). 3. Underneath it, read "frontend view restriction". ### "Edit permissions required" 1. Go to '`/admin/cms/globalpagepermissions/add`. 2. Add permission for user or group: 1. Check "Can publish". 2. Check nothing else. 4. Submit 5. See error "Users can't […] Edit permissions required." ## Expected behaviour Text that has less interpretations, and such that the correct interpretation is easy to determine. ### "View restricted" Because it actually means `not can_view` ([ref.](https://django-cmsworkspace.slack.com/archives/C01EBCEK49E/p1692688566786649?thread_ts=1692654745.963519&cid=C01EBCEK49E)), maybe something like: > Can not view restricted pages. But, what are "restricted pages"? ### "frontend view restriction" Because it actually describes `not can_view` ([ref.](https://django-cmsworkspace.slack.com/archives/C01EBCEK49E/p1692688566786649?thread_ts=1692654745.963519&cid=C01EBCEK49E)), mayeb soemthing like: > Hides restricted pages from selected user/group. But, what are "restricted pages"? But how to keep "Can edit" in sync with the label text to which it refers? ### "[…] Edit permissions required" Maybe, > Ensure user has "Can edit" permission But how to keep "Can edit" in sync with the label text to which it refers? ## Actual behaviour ### "View restricted" Label text "View restricted" is unclear because of multiple interpretations: - "View (as a verb) restricted [what]". - "View [of … what … is] restricted". ### "frontend view restriction" Help text "frontend view restriction" is unclear because of it creates more questions than it answers: - There is a restriction? - This makes a restriction? - Is the restriction active when checked or not checked? - Can I restrict a backend view from this page? ### "[…] Edit permissions required" Error text "Edit permissions required" is unclear because of multiple interpretations: - "Edit permissions [are] required." - "Edit (as a verb) [the] permissions [that are] required." ## Screenshots | View restricted | frontend view restriction | […] Edit permissions required | | - | - | - | | ![View restricted](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/assets/62723358/4aff7269-df28-451f-a8bf-45a1354b41f7) | ![frontend view restriction](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/assets/62723358/ad7c3ea7-b779-4ab9-a7f8-4bd970bf94ef) | | ## Additional information (CMS/Python/Django versions) - Django CMS: 3.8.0 - Django: 3.2 - Python: 1.4.0 ## Do you want to help fix this issue? * Yes, I want to help fix this issue and I will join #workgroup-pr-review on [Slack](https://www.django-cms.org/slack) to confirm with the community that a PR is welcome. * Maybe, and if Yes, then I agree to the above. * [x] No, I only want to report the issue.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: [BUG] Special characters in page title
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

If a page title contains special characters, such as `&`, then this character is rendered as HTML-entity, for instance `&`.
In browser tabs this does not look right.


## Steps to reproduce

* Create a page template where the page title is used. This usually is done by adding

```html
…
<meta>
  {% page_attribute "page_title" as page_title %}
  <title>{{ page_title}}</title>
  …
</meta>
…
```


* Create or edit a page and use `A & B` as the page title.
* Load the page.

The browser tab shows `A & B`.

## Expected behaviour

The browser tab should show `A & B` as page title.


## Do you want to help fix this issue?

By patching the templatetag `cms.templatetags.cms_tags.PageAttribute` and [not escaping the value](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/fa7b89ceec3bd22e031be8e9cf2328a3f9434b12/cms/templatetags/cms_tags.py#L411), this can be fixed easily. However, I don't know what security implications this fix may have.

I would exempt escaping the string, whenever the name is `page_title`, just as we do it with values of type `datetime`.

Any objections to this?


* [x] Yes, I want to help fix this issue and I will join #workgroup-pr-review on [Slack](https://www.django-cms.org/slack) to confirm with the community that a PR is welcome. 
* [ ] No, I only want to report the issue.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: fix: Versioning-safe implementation of placeholder inheritance
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

The `ContentRenderer.render_page_placeholders` implementation is not versioning-safe, i.e. assumes that there is exactly one `PageContent` object per `Page` and language. This PR improves the implementation using the `admin_manager`.

This will allow `{% placeholder "my_placeholder" inherit %}` to also work with versioned page contents, such as provided by djangocms-versioning. (For it to actually work with djangocms-versioning, however, an additional change to djangocms-versioning is needed, to not deactivate the inherit functionality.)

Results with djangocms-versioning:
* When rendered at the URL (i.e. public endpoint): The placeholder only inherits from also public placeholders
* When previewed: The placeholder inherits from the latest parent placeholder (i.e. public or draft)
* When edited: Inherited placeholders are empty to allow for adding content

Then changes are covered by tests. Additional tests need to go into djangocms-versioning if the inheritance feature is activated again.

nodes.title: Support Content-Security-Policy without "script-src unsafe-inline"
nodes.body:
Django 1.10 lands support for running the admin with a Content-Security-Policy without "script-src unsafe-inline" applied. This allows the django admin to be completely immune from XSS attacks.

Django CMS should follow suit and remove all inline JavaScript. Replacing large blocks of JS with `<script src={% static 'path/to/old_inlines/eg.js' %}></script>` and `<script>var foo = {{bar}}></script>` with:

``` js
# path/to/fooUsage.js
window.foo = $('#django-cms-foo').data('foo');
```

``` html
<script id='django-cms-foo' src={% static 'path/to/fooUsuage.js' %} data-foo={{ bar }}></script>
```

nodes.title: [BUG] Data bridge does not update frontend-editable models
nodes.body:
<!--
Please fill in each section below, otherwise, your issue will be closed.
This info allows django CMS maintainers to diagnose (and fix!) your issue
as quickly as possible.
-->

## Description

When adding a plugin or editing a plugin the so-called "data bridge" updates the frontend editor of django CMS by providing changes in the plugin tree. To the frontend, three "types" of plugins are important: 
* Regular plugins (corresponding to a `CMSPlugin`model object)
* Placeholders (which is where the regular plugins live)
* General plugins (which connect some part of a template to a Django model object. Double-clicking it opens a modal to edit the object) - see https://docs.django-cms.org/en/latest/how_to/06-frontend_models.html

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: [BUG] cms middleware defeats ASGI adaptation
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

Django async support adapts synchronous middleware to an asynchronous middleware stack automagically.  It does that by assuming it's synchronous and testing for async.  Subclassing MiddlewareMixin makes that test positive.  However, some cms middleware then overrides \_\_call\_\_, which django does not adapt, causing it to fail.

Of the five middlewares provided, LanguageCookieMiddleware and CurrentUserMiddleware both suffer from this.

## Steps to reproduce

Run django-cms on an ASGI server (uvicorn in my case).

## Expected behaviour

Django async support allows non-async django-cms to run alongside async-aware apps.

## Actual behaviour

Failure is immediate if LanguageCookieMiddleware is installed:

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: fix: apphooks at endpoints
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

Apphooks are available on site but currently not at the edit or preview endpoints: If they exists the page's page contents is shown/offered for editing. IMHO this might be confusing for users since those page contents are shadowed by the apphook on the public site.

This PR catches apphooks in the preview/edit views of the respective endpoints and replaces the page by the apphook's view (if existent else an error page is shown).

This should improve usability when navigating sites with apphooks in preview mode.

## Demo

Select view on an app hooked page content in the page tree gets you to the preview endpoint not triggering the app hook. **Expected behaviour: show the app hook already at the preview endpoint**.

![no-apphook](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16904477/221154324-27b9f726-d729-480f-ab8a-6ec6d5b22160.gif)



## Additional information

<!--
Add here links to existing issues or conversation from GitHub
or any other resource.
-->

* If app hooks need to detect the url (e.g. to determine the relevant namespace) they can do so by checking `request.toolbar.path_info`. `request.path_info` will point to the preview endpoint and **not** resolve to the correct namespace. Consequently, namespaced app hooks will potentially have to adjust their code base to detect their namespace. 
* The redundancy in `render_object_edit` and `render_objects_preview` in `cms/views.py` has been factored out with `render_object_endpoint`

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: fix: create page wizard fails with Asian page titles/unicode slugs
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

This PR ports #7565 to version 4.

Django CMS supports unihandecode.js slug generation (if [configured](https://docs.django-cms.org/en/latest/reference/configuration.html?highlight=UNIHANDECODE#unicode-support-for-automated-slugs) in the settings). This PR resolves the following issues

* Unihandecode settings were ignored by the create page wizard
* Create page wizard crashed if unicode slugs were entered manually (#7564) (except for the root page)
* Misleading validation messages if non-ascii slugs were entered in the page settings

The root cause were inconsistent form validations and unihandecode being hard-wired into the page settings template while the wizard uses a custom SlugWidget:
* The SlugWidget moved into the AddPage/ChangePage forms
* unihandecode.js is loaded by the widget, not a form template: Thus it is available in both the page settings and create page wizard.
* Validation is handled by Django's SlugField validators and not inconsistently by different django CMS forms.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: fix: validate endpoint languages and redirect if not editable
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

This PR ensures that content object endpoints are rendered in the language of the content object, if it has one defined (using its `language` property).  
* English content objects have `/en/admin/placeholder/...` as path
* Italian content objects have `/it/admin/placeholder/..` as path

It also completes the toolbar API by adding a `object_is_editable` method which checks if the toolbar object has a `is_editable` property as set, e.g., by djangocms_versioning.

The Page menu only offers edit page if the page content object is editable (prevents an undefined state as described in https://github.com/django-cms/djangocms-versioning/issues/354).

The edit endpoint will redirect to the preview endpoint if a toolbar object is not editable, solving https://github.com/django-cms/djangocms-versioning/issues/355 and https://github.com/django-cms/djangocms-versioning/issues/337

Finally, optimizes the page rendering, preventing detecting the selected language multiple times.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: Fixed #6289 -- Don't fail silently on templates with variable extends
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
Fixed #6289

This fixes the regression raised when using an extends node with a variable and default.
Note that using a variable alone like `{% extends SOMETHING %}` is still not supported as per https://github.com/divio/django-cms/issues/1847 and will raise a `SyntaxError`.

The only supported cases are:

`{% extends "explicit.html" %}` or `{% extends SOMETHING|default:"explicit.html" %}`.

On that last case, is important to note that it can lead to unexpected results because when the cms scans it, it will **always** default to `explicit.html` but when the page is rendered and the correct context is passed, then the template might use `SOMETHING`, while the structure placeholders come from `explicit.html`.

Ideally we should raise a warning or prevent these templates all-together.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: Menu cache keys are not expiring correctly
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
The menu cache works by creating a unique cache key for each user, site & language combo.
If the user is not logged in, then the key is unique for site and language only.

Because these keys are created for each user, the cms stores a reference to the keys in the database under the model `CacheKey`, this allows the cms to delete all cached entries when something changes, without having to recompute the key for every user.

When a page is requested, the cms will load the menu which as a first step checks if the cache key for this user exists in the cache server, if it does then it will immediately return the result, otherwise it will discover and process all menu nodes and then store the nodes in the cache server **and** create a reference to the key used on the cache server, in the `CacheKey` model.

This pattern can lead to a case where if the cache key does not exist in the database (`CacheKey` model) but it exists in the cache server, any content that is there will be served, even though it could be outdated.

Normally, when a page is published or changed, the cms will clear the cache.
Clearing the cache involves getting all keys from the `CacheKey` model and deleting each one through django's cache api.

But there is a problem where the keys go out of sync, thus recreating the scenario mentioned above.

This problem was introduced by https://github.com/divio/django-cms/pull/1252, where cache keys in the database are cleared but their counterpart in the cache server are not.

To reproduce this, depending on the machine used, make two requests at the same time and make a third one exactly one second after the first two.

<!--

## Description

In Django CMS 3 when you configured a page as a redirect to another page (Page > Advanced Settings) the page showed a message _"This page has no preview! It is being redirected to: <path>"_ whenever you opened it in the frontend while being logged in. 

In Django CMS 4 this message is no longer available. When you open a redirecting-page it shows the (most likely empty) page if you are in the editing mode or it redirects to the configured target page if you are in preview mode. So while being in the editing mode, you don't get any indication that a redirect has been configured for the current page which seems a source for confusion for CMS editors.


## Suggested behavior

My suggestion is to reintroduce a similar behavior as in Django CMS 3. The message _"This page has no preview! (...)"_ should be displayed in both editing- **and** preview-mode and by that making it easier to edit the redirecting page.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: feat: Performant permission calculation for pages
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

With permissions by page activated, the CMS needs to traverse the page tree to find permissions which apply to a specific page. For each permission, django CMS calculates the list of page IDs it applies to. This calculation is cached.

For projects with large numbers of pages (>> 1,000) these calculations generate long lists of IDs and even using the cached calculations impacts responsiveness.

This PR noticeably improves the responsiveness when working with large page trees.

This PR optimizes the calculation of permission based on a page's `path` (actually a tuple `grant_on` and `path`, where the `grant_on` code defines if the permission applies to the page itself, its direct children, and/or all of its descendants). This makes both calculating the permissions and evaluating the cached permissions from O(n) to O(1) (n being the number of pages) (but stays O(m) for m being the number of permissions granted).

Thanks to @jrief for testing.
@Aiden-RC Please be invited to test and comment!

Thanks to @vinitkumar for testing a backport to django CMS 3.11.

## Deprecations

This PR deprecates some (not officially documented) utility functions in `cms.utils.page.permissions` which are replaced by their counterparts getting the permission tuples, e.g., `get_add_perm_tuples`:
* get_add_ids
* get_change_ids
* get_change_advanced_settings_ids
* get_change_permissions_ids
* get_delete_ids
* get_move_page_ids
* get_publish_ids
* get_view_ids

It also deprecates the `get_page_ids` method of the `cms.models.PagePermissions` model.

Their database access is not efficient and redundant.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: Publishing updates to home/root page prefixes child public page paths with "%2F"
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
### Summary
The extra slash is only added when both the parent and child page have already been published. The 
draft version of the child page still has the correct path 
Steps to recreate:

1. Create a new page at the root and set as the home page. Use default settings.
2. Publish home page
3. Create a sub-page off the root with a simple title and slug (ex. Archer, archer)
4. Publish sub-page and note its public url. In this case "localhost/archer"
5. Make a change to the home page such updating title or adding a plugin
6. Publish the homepage

### Expected behavior
The public path of child pages should not change

### Actual behavior
As a logged out public user go to localhost/archer and you will get a 404. If you have a menu on your home page it will show the url for the subpage as "/%2Farcher"

### Environment

* Python version: 3.6.6
* Django version: 1.11.10
* django CMS version: 3.5.1 and 3.5.0

### What to Fix
The culprit appears to be this line of code: https://github.com/divio/django-cms/blob/3.5.1/cms/models/pagemodel.py#L1121

I believe fixing is as easy as comparing if base == '/' and excluding the '/'. Will try to confirm.

4. Publish sub-page and note its public url. In this case "localhost/archer"
5. Make a change to the home page such updating title or adding a plugin
6. Publish the homepage

### Expected behavior
The public path of child pages should not change

### Actual behavior
As a logged out public user go to localhost/archer and you will get a 404. If you have a menu on your home page it will show the url for the subpage as "/%2Farcher"

### Environment

* Python version: 3.6.6
* Django version: 1.11.10
* django CMS version: 3.5.1 and 3.5.0

### What to Fix
The culprit appears to be this line of code: https://github.com/divio/django-cms/blob/3.5.1/cms/models/pagemodel.py#L1121

I believe fixing is as easy as comparing if base == '/' and excluding the '/'. Will try to confirm.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

Historically, django CMS has used a python cache on model level for page content objects: `page.page_content_cache`.

Since django CMS 4., this cache is filled either with user-visible objects (using the default `objects` manager) or with admin-visible objects, using the `admin_manager` manager. Since each request is, either from the user side or the admin side, this same cache can be used to hold different sets of page content objects. A side effect, however, lead to some page titles in fallback languages not to be shown in the page tree.

It turns out, however, that this was not consistently done, leading to unnecessary cache misses. 

This PR splits the caches into `page_content_cache`(traditional, user-facing) and `admin_content_cache` for the page admin, to make sure no side effects can happen.

This improves the cache hits and reduces the number of database hits for the page tree effectively removing a hidden N+1 issue. The response time should improve by 20%+ (tested with local sqlite).

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: Impossible to redirect to home when not using i18n_patterns
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
### Summary

I have a site where I don't need international URLs, so I disabled them by not using `i18n_patterns` in `urls.py`.

Let's say I have two cms pages:

* Home (path / without language prefix)
* Foo (path /foo and also without language prefix)

In the advanced settings of Foo, I can select the entry "Home (/)" in the redirect field. After submitting the form, I get the following error: "Enter a valid URL."

The redirect field (`PageSmartLinkField`) uses `validate_url`. `validate_url` gets `value='/'` and calls `RegexValidator(regex=relative_url_regex)(value)`. I think the issue is that `relative_url_regex` does not match the path `/`. It only matches paths like e.g. `/foo`.

I suggest to modify `relative_url_regex` so that it also matches `/` and `./` since these are valid paths.


### Expected behaviour

Redirect field accepts `/`.

#### Actual behaviour

Redirect field does not accept `/`. The error "Enter a valid URL." is shown.

#### Environment

* Python version: 3.6.1
* Django version: 1.10.7
* django CMS version: 3.4.3

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

**This PR does not change any functionality!**

It just fixes two anti-patterns in django-CMS:

`force_str(_("…some text…"))` is completely useless because it forces to stringify a proxy object. A better and faster way is to use `gettext("…some text…")` directly.

`HttpResponse(json.dumps(content), content_type="application/json")` probably is a legacy statement. Django introduced `JsonResponse` many versions ago.


## Related resources

We discussed about this during one of our biweekly meetings.

## Description

Method `cms.site_map.CMSSiteMap.lastmod` returns the wrong date for the given page.


## Steps to reproduce

* Enable sitemaps for your CMS.
* Navigate to the sitemaps page.
* Compare the tag `<lastmod>…</lastmod>` with the latest published page content of the given page.

## Expected behaviour

`<lastmod>…</lastmod>` should contain `page_content.changed_date`


## Actual behaviour

`<lastmod>…</lastmod>` contains `page.changed_date`


## Additional information (CMS/Python/Django versions)

CMS 4.1.1

## Do you want to help fix this issue?

The fix is quite simple. Therefore I just want to ask, if this fix would be accepted:

change method

```python

class CMSSitemap(Sitemap):
    …
    def lastmod(self, page_url):
        return page_url.page.get_content_obj(page_url.language).changed_date
```

This btw. causes an N+1 issue. Therefore also change method

```python

class CMSSitemap(Sitemap):
    …
    def items(self) -> QuerySet:
        …
        return (
            …
            .prefetch_related("page__pagecontent_set")
        )
```

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: fix: Language tabs didn't show existing content due to caching issue
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

This PR resolves issue #8044 by not setting the `admin_content_cache` when calling `get_object`. Doing so resulted in partial caches being present for only the currently selected language, meaning that any use of the cache would yield an `EmptyPageContent` object instead of the actual content.

This breaks the language tabs inside the page edit form. Not setting the cache partially now triggers the `set_admin_content_cache` method and resolves this issue.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

Consider the following scenario: we got a multi-language site using the languages English (en) and German (de). 

We currently got a page which only exists in the German (de) version. Therefore, we only have a published `PageContent` object for this page in German.

If we change the language switch inside the `PageContent` admin list view (the one on top, just beside the "Main Navigation" label) to `English (en)`, we can see the title of the German Page with a "(de)" behind it. We can then click on the grey circle to create the english version of the page. This all works flawlessly.

However, suppose we have a page which is published in both versions. We now click on the page content settings on the German version and then use the language tab on top of the form to switch the language to English.
This results in an empty form without title, slug or anything that the *already existing english version of this page* provides. If we continue to fill out the form and save it, we can create an inconsistent state inside the DB because the `PageUrl` objects now return 2 results for the english page version. 

If we look at the `get_urls()` method of this page, we can see that the English version now has 2 PageUrl objects:

`<QuerySet [<PageUrl: english-testpage (en)>, <PageUrl: deutsche-testseite-translated (de)>, <PageUrl: adskjfhgdskjfhdsakjh (en)>]>`

If we then select the language with 2 `PageUrl` objects in the `PageContent` list view and try to edit it, we get an error:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):

    response = get_response(request)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/core/handlers/base.py", line 197, in _get_response
    response = wrapped_callback(request, *callback_args, **callback_kwargs)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/contrib/admin/options.py", line 688, in wrapper
    return self.admin_site.admin_view(view)(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/utils/decorators.py", line 134, in _wrapper_view
    response = view_func(request, *args, **kwargs)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/views/decorators/cache.py", line 62, in _wrapper_view_func
    response = view_func(request, *args, **kwargs)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/contrib/admin/sites.py", line 242, in inner
    return view(request, *args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/cms/admin/pageadmin.py", line 981, in change_view
    return super().change_view(request, object_id, form_url=form_url, extra_context=context)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/contrib/admin/options.py", line 1889, in change_view
    return self.changeform_view(request, object_id, form_url, extra_context)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/utils/decorators.py", line 46, in _wrapper
    return bound_method(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/utils/decorators.py", line 134, in _wrapper_view
    response = view_func(request, *args, **kwargs)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/contrib/admin/options.py", line 1747, in changeform_view
    return self._changeform_view(request, object_id, form_url, extra_context)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/contrib/admin/options.py", line 1819, in _changeform_view
    form = ModelForm(instance=obj)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/cms/admin/forms.py", line 578, in __init__
    self.url_obj = self.instance.page.get_url(self._language)
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/cms/models/pagemodel.py", line 782, in get_url
    return self.get_urls().get(language=language)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/django/db/models/query.py", line 640, in get
    raise self.model.MultipleObjectsReturned(
    ^

Exception Type: MultipleObjectsReturned at /de/admin/cms/pagecontent/362/change/
Exception Value: get() returned more than one PageUrl -- it returned 2!
```

This is really unexpected because we get an explicit option to edit page contents in more than one way and depending on which way you choose you may end up destroying the integrity of your pages.


## Steps to reproduce

Follow the steps above.

## Expected behaviour

Page Content always get correctly fetched and edited without destroying the consistency of the DB

## Actual behaviour

See above.

## Screenshots

Not really applicable, the reproduction is too complex to convey through screenshots.

## Additional information (CMS/Python/Django versions)
Python 3.11
Django 4.2
djangoCMS 4.1.3

## Do you want to help fix this issue?

Imo, this can only be resolved in two ways: 
1) fix the edit view of page content objects so that using the tab select correctly fetches existing page information and edits it as expected (just the way it did in djangoCMS 3) or
2) completely disable the tab selectors inside the page content edit view so that you NEED to use the language select inside the list view.

I know this may seem hard to fathom and especially hard to reproduce, so if anyone needs clarification or a short demo I am always available to hop on a quick Discord call.

So yes, I'd like to help but I can't really dig through djangoCMS internals right now and create a PR. Always happy to review them by testing however :)

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: feat: Add live-url url query parameter to PageContent cms Preview and Edit endpoints
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

A new feature added to v4 Preview and Edit endpoints. Currently there’s no way of knowing what the current pages live url is like you used to be able to with 3.x using ?edit, this new feature (off by default) adds a query string parameter to the preview and edit endpoints.

Without the new feature enabled
Preview endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8000/en/admin/cms/placeholder/object/3/preview/372/
Edit endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8000/en/admin/cms/placeholder/object/3/edit/372/
Live url: /en/blog/

With the new feature enabled
Preview endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8000/en/admin/cms/placeholder/object/3/preview/372/?live-url=/en/blog/
Edit endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8000/en/admin/cms/placeholder/object/3/edit/372/?live-url=/en/blog/
Live url: /en/blog/

This PR introduces two settings, CMS_ENDPOINT_LIVE_URL_QUERYSTRING_PARAM_ENABLED and CMS_ENDPOINT_LIVE_URL_QUERYSTRING_PARAM. With the former set True, and a param (as a string) provided with the latter, the preview and edit endpoints for PageContent will append the live-url as a query string parameter.

rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.title: feat: Re-introduce page-level publish permission just as in v4.0
rest::/repos/django-cms/django-cms/issue.body:
## Description

In django CMS version 4.1 the `can_publish` permission was removed. With the next release of djangocms-versioning it will support low-level publication permissions if the versioned content model supports it.

This PR restores the `can_publish` permissions and its test as it was available in django CMS 4.0.

Tests have been restored, too.

A (no-op) squashed migration was added to ensure that publish permissions are not lost during migration processes:
* `0035` removes page publish permissions (released in 4.1.0)
* `0036` adds the page publish permissions back
* Squashed migration `0035` replaces `0035` and `0036` with a no-op

I want to merge this change because it prevents issue where using WebhookDelete mutation while tasks that create EventDeliveryAttempt are queued resulted in IntegrityError.

The most simple resolution was to deactivate Webhook before deleting it in mutation. send_webhook_request_async task is checking if webhook is_active so this should prevent this situation.

Things to discuss:
⚠️ There is a small window for this solution to fail - when Webhook deactivation will happen between the is_active check and attempt creating/updating in send_webhook_request_async task. I'm not quite sure how to handle this case. Should I add more webhook activity checks inside send_webhook_request_async task or maybe catch this edge-case exception to fail gracefully? Any ideas?

Second thing: Do we want to do the sam analogically for deleting App? (deactivate webhook in app deletion)

nodes.title: Bug: Missing "app id" in app extension token
nodes.body:
### What are you trying to achieve?

App (via app-sdk) is checking `app` field in user JWT token (sent from dashboard, via postmessage to appbridge) and compares it to registered app ID (that app persists). If app ID is different, app is rejecting the call.

However, there are also extensions that have their own token (they can have different permissions). **This token lacks `app` field**. 

For app, extension is its part, so its expected to have app ID in the token as well. Otherwise, app would require to persist all registered extensions to work, which is quite hard to implement.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

## App token payload

```json
{
  "iat": 1679048767,
  "owner": "saleor",
  "iss": "https://automation-dashboard.staging.saleor.cloud/graphql/",
  "exp": 1679135167,
  "token": "M2irFmzVASR3",
  "email": "testers+dashboard@saleor.io",
  "type": "thirdparty",
  "user_id": "VXNlcjoxMDMz",
  "is_staff": true,
  "app": "QXBwOjY0",
  "permissions": [
    "MANAGE_PRODUCTS"
  ],
  "user_permissions": [
    "MANAGE_GIFT_CARD",
    "MANAGE_MENUS",
    "MANAGE_PAGES",
    "MANAGE_PAGE_TYPES_AND_ATTRIBUTES",
    "MANAGE_PLUGINS",
    "MANAGE_TAXES",
    "MANAGE_USERS",
    "MANAGE_CHECKOUTS",
    "MANAGE_PRODUCT_TYPES_AND_ATTRIBUTES",
    "MANAGE_TRANSLATIONS",
    "MANAGE_APPS",
    "MANAGE_OBSERVABILITY",
    "MANAGE_STAFF",
    "HANDLE_TAXES",
    "MANAGE_CHANNELS",
    "HANDLE_CHECKOUTS",
    "MANAGE_SETTINGS",
    "HANDLE_PAYMENTS",
    "MANAGE_ORDERS",
    "MANAGE_PRODUCTS",
    "MANAGE_SHIPPING",
    "MANAGE_DISCOUNTS",
    "IMPERSONATE_USER"
  ]
}
```


## Extension token payload

```json
  "owner": "saleor",
  "iss": "https://automation-dashboard.staging.saleor.cloud/graphql/",
  "exp": 1679137338,
  "token": "M2irFmzVASR3",
  "email": "testers+dashboard@saleor.io",
  "type": "thirdparty",
  "user_id": "VXNlcjoxMDMz",
  "is_staff": true,
  "app_extension": "QXBwRXh0ZW5zaW9uOjQy",
  "permissions": [],
  "user_permissions": [
    "MANAGE_GIFT_CARD",
    "MANAGE_MENUS",
    "MANAGE_PAGES",
    "MANAGE_PAGE_TYPES_AND_ATTRIBUTES",
    "MANAGE_PLUGINS",
    "MANAGE_TAXES",
    "MANAGE_USERS",
    "MANAGE_CHECKOUTS",
    "MANAGE_PRODUCT_TYPES_AND_ATTRIBUTES",
    "MANAGE_TRANSLATIONS",
    "MANAGE_APPS",
    "MANAGE_OBSERVABILITY",
    "MANAGE_STAFF",
    "HANDLE_TAXES",
    "MANAGE_CHANNELS",
    "HANDLE_CHECKOUTS",
    "MANAGE_SETTINGS",
    "HANDLE_PAYMENTS",
    "MANAGE_ORDERS",
    "MANAGE_PRODUCTS",
    "MANAGE_SHIPPING",
    "MANAGE_DISCOUNTS",
    "IMPERSONATE_USER"
  ]
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

Extension token should contain `app` field

### Logs

_No response_

### Environment

Saleor version: …
OS and version: …

Additionally, I also cleaned up the `get_base_objects` method, to reduce the `OR` operations in generated DB query

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/11132.title: Bug: The `checkoutPaymentCreate` can be run during `checkoutComplete` performing
rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/11132.body:
### What are you trying to achieve?

The `checkoutPaymentCreate` can be run during `checkoutComplete` performing, it can cause the deactivation of the payment that is currently performed in the `checkoutComplete` mutation - we should prevent such a situation.


### Steps to reproduce the problem

It can be hard to reproduce as the `checkoutPaymentCreate` mutation need to be called during `process_payment` calls in `checkoutComplete` mutation, but the steps are:
1. Create checkout
2. Update shipping method if needed
3. Run `checkoutPaymentCreate` the payment object will be created
4. Run zcheckoutComplete` mutation
5. In the meantime, when waiting for a response from the gateway, run `checkoutPaymentCreate` once again.
6. It should end up with a situation that the payment was process for inactive payment, the second uncharged payment will be active.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40886528/199694038-feb5c5fb-a16d-47d3-bb0e-5326badfeeee.png)


### What did you expect to happen?

Running `checkoutPaymentCreate` should be blocked when `checkoutComplete` is run.

### Logs

_No response_

### Environment

Saleor version: 3.1+

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/11133.title: Bug: The `CheckoutPaymentCreate` can be run multiple times in the same time for the checkout
rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/11133.body:
### What are you trying to achieve?

The `CheckoutPaymentCreate` can be run multiple times in the same time for the checkout. As the result we end up with multiple active payments. The solution for blocking multiple active payment creations should be introduced.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Run `CheckoutPaymentCreate` for the checkout multiple times at the same time.
2. The `Payment.MultipleObjectsReturned` error is rasied
 


### What did you expect to happen?

The current payment cancelation and new payment creation should happen in the transaction.

### Logs

Sentry issue: https://sentry.io/organizations/saleor/issues/3708155945/?project=6417854&referrer=slack

### Environment

Saleor version: 3.1+

nodes.title: Add `FULFILLMENT_TRACKING_NUMBER_UPDATED` webhook
nodes.body:
Add `FULFILLMENT_TRACKING_NUMBER_UPDATED` webhook to allow notifying listeners about the changed tracking number of the fulfillment. The event should be run in the following cases:
- when the tracking number is set in the `fulfillmentUpdateTracking` mutation
- when the tracking number is set in the `orderFulfill` mutation

Payload: 

```graphql
type FulfillmentTrackingNumberUpdated implements Event @doc(category: "Orders") {
  issuedAt: DateTime
  version: String
  issuingPrincipal: IssuingPrincipal
  recipient: App
  fulfillment: Fulfillment
  order: Order
}
```

Required permission: `MANAGE_ORDERS`

Notes:
- This webhook will replace the `ORDER_FULFILLMENT_UPDATE` action event in the `NOTIFY` webhook.
- There is already a `tracking_number_updated` hook in the plugin manager used for the `np-atobarai` payment plugin.

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/18539.title: Fix automatic checkout completion
rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/18539.body:
Port of https://github.com/saleor/saleor/pull/18528

- Extended `CheckoutSettingsInput` with a new `automatic_completion` field, replacing and deprecating `automatically_complete_fully_paid_checkouts`.
- `automatic_completion` input now supports:
  - `enabled` — toggles automatic checkout completion.
  - `delay` — optional delay before completion; defaults to a predefined value when omitted.
  - `cut_off_date` — defines the earliest checkout timestamp eligible for automatic completion; defaults to the current time.
- These settings can now be defined in both `channelCreate` and `channelUpdate`.
- For existing channels with automatic completion enabled, `delay` defaults to `0`.
- When switching automatic completion from `True` → `False`, the `delay` and `cut_off_date` is cleared.
- When switching from `False` → `True` without providing a `delay` or `cut_off_date`, the default delay is applied.

labels.name: test deployment
labels.description: Deploy test environment for pull request

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/9343.body:
This PR adds a new mutation that will be used in the new checkout flow. New checkout flow will allow us to a more flexible handle payment process. The basic assumption is: that we have a separate Saleor App that is responsible for handling a payment process. This allows us to handle different cases like `payment then order`, `order then payment`, `payment then order then payment`, `multiple payments`, etc. The new mutation will be responsible for creating order from checkout. Quick things that I believe it is good to raise: - **PR is huge but two of the biggest files are a port of tests from checkout complete files.** - Mutation `OrderCreateFromCheckout` will require expected permission. - Logic for converting a checkout into an order `(complete_checkout.py)` is refactored logic that was called in `CheckoutComplete) mutation. - Fixme will be handled in separate PR - The mutation has its own group of possible errors. This is a way, for better handling errors on frontend side. To give you more context for this new flow, I've added some charts that explain the concept. ### Case: Order before payment ```mermaid sequenceDiagram Customer->>+Checkout App: Finalize an order rect rgb(162, 162, 162) Note over Checkout App, Saleor: Covered part by this PR Checkout App ->>+ Saleor: Create order from checkout Saleor -->>- Checkout App: Unpaid order end Checkout App-->>-Customer: Order Customer ->>+ Checkout App: Process payment Checkout App ->>+ Payment provider: Process payment for order Payment provider -->>- Checkout App: Payment with proper status Checkout App ->>+ Saleor: Create payment for order Saleor -->>- Checkout App: Payment created and
attached to order Checkout App -->>- Customer: Order paid ``` ### Case: Payment before order ```mermaid sequenceDiagram Customer ->>+ Checkout App: Process payment Checkout App ->>+ Payment provider: Process payment for checkout Payment provider -->>- Checkout App: Payment with proper status Checkout App ->>+ Saleor: Create payment for checkout Saleor -->>- Checkout App: Payment created and
attached to checkout Checkout App -->>- Customer: Payment paid Customer->>+Checkout App: Conver checkout into an order rect rgb(162, 162, 162) Note over Checkout App, Saleor: Covered part by this PR Checkout App ->>+ Saleor: Create order from checkout Saleor ->> Saleor: Attach checkout's payments to order Saleor -->>- Checkout App: Paid order end Checkout App-->>-Customer: Order ```

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/15748.title: Optimize validate_draft_order function to run less queries
rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/15748.body:
The `validate_draft_order` function is used in two queries and one mutation. In each case, it runs a lot of duplicated queries due to not properly using dataloaders and accessing not prefetched data via implicit DB queries. This PR partially improves it and loads order lines via dataloader, which are then passed around via arguments. 

There are still many queries to optimize here but it already improved a lot. Example: fetching 5 draft orders and `errors` field:
```
{
  draftOrders(first:5) {
    edges {
      node {
        id
        errors {
          field
          message
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Before: 48 queries
After: 19 queries

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/18571.title: Remove mount, target and options from AppExtension

labels.name: approved-breaking-change
labels.description: PRs with this label have approved breaking changes in the GraphQL schema

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/18571.body:
## Summary
Removes deprecated fields `mount`, `target`, and `options` from `AppExtension` and `AppManifestExtension` GraphQL types. These fields were deprecated in favor of `mountName`, `targetName`, and `settings` which were introduced in 3.22. The Dashboard has already migrated to use the new fields.

## Breaking Changes


### Removed from GraphQL schema:
- `AppExtension.mount` → use `AppExtension.mountName`
- `AppExtension.target` → use `AppExtension.targetName`
- `AppExtension.options` → use `AppExtension.settings`
- `AppManifestExtension.mount` → use `AppManifestExtension.mountName`
- `AppManifestExtension.target` → use `AppManifestExtension.targetName`
- `AppManifestExtension.options` → use `AppManifestExtension.settings`
- `AppExtensionFilterInput.mount` → use `AppExtensionFilterInput.mountName`
- `AppExtensionFilterInput.target` → use `AppExtensionFilterInput.targetName`
- `AppExtensionMountEnum` type
- `AppExtensionTargetEnum` type

## Changes
- Removed deprecated fields from GraphQL types and filters
- Removed enum types `AppExtensionMountEnum` and `AppExtensionTargetEnum`
- Updated all tests to use new field names
- Updated changelog with breaking change notice

## Migration
API consumers should update their queries to use the replacement fields introduced in 3.22:
- `mount` → `mountName` (returns string instead of enum)
- `target` → `targetName` (returns string instead of enum)
- `options` → `settings` (returns JSON object)

**Files changed:** 12 files (+70/-407 lines)

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/19615.title: Fix DB locks - never-evaluated `select_for_update` querysets
rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/19615.body:
While working on other stuff, I found locking code where the `select_for_update` queryset was built and assigned but never evaluated. Querysets are lazy, so no SQL ran at all - no `FOR UPDATE` lock was taken and the `bulk_update` that followed ran unlocked, in arbitrary row order (deadlock risk against other writers)

- Fixed by forcing evaluation with `list(...)` inside the transaction
- Added the `assert_locks_rows_before_write` fixture, which asserts an ordered
  `FOR UPDATE` query runs before the `UPDATE` - to catch missing locks
- Documented the pitfall in `AGENTS.md`

nodes.title: Bug: Stock update webhook is not triggered
nodes.body:
### What are you trying to achieve?

Get notified when variant is out of stock

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Create a new variant with quantity of 0
OUT_OF_STOCK webhook was sent
2. Add a quantity of 5
BACK_IN_STOCK webhook was sent
5. I've made two orders (with 3 quantity and 2 quantity) (stocks at this moment - allocated 5, quantity 5)
6. OUT_OF_STOCK webhook was sent
7. I added another 10 items to the stock (allocated 5, quantity 15)

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect to BACK_IN_STOCK webhook to be sent, but it's not. The only workaround I've found is to set quantity to 0 and then set it to 15 in step 7.


### Logs

_No response_

### Environment

dashboard v3.7.9
core v3.7.27

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/16986.title: Recalculate prices even when tax app returns empty data.
rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/16986.body:
I want to merge this change to revert the change introduced in https://github.com/saleor/saleor/pull/16696. Skipping price assignment for tax app strategy is redundant as `TaxableObjectLine` return base prices, which don't include order-level discounts anyway.

When taxes are calculated with tax app, we update prices with data received from tax app. In case of tax data is empty (ie. lack of address) we currently skip all the calculation. This PR ensure we calculate at least untaxed values. 

This PR also covers order price calculation with tax app strategy path with tests.

rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/17406.title: Properly emit `ProductVariantMetadataUpdated` from `ProductVariantUpdate`
rest::/repos/saleor/saleor/issues/17406.body:
I want to merge this change because

Before:
- `productVariantUpdate` executed with `metadata` or `privateMetadata` did not emit `ProductVariantMetadataUpdated` event
- `metadataUpdate` properly emitted this event

After
- `productVariantUpdate` now emits `ProductVariantMetadataUpdated` if metadata field was used (and actually changed).
- `ProductVariantMetadataUpdated` is not emitted if metadata was not provided or not changed in DB
- `metadataUpdate` behaves without change
